_doc: Lookup key: schoolId|round|reason, with schoolName|round|reason as a fallback for deterministic seed data whose generated IDs change. The verify script uses this to override the default UNREVIEWED classification on manualReview rows. Add new entries when verify:counselor-data-quality flags new anomalies; do not edit a classification without re-reviewing the underlying CDS data.

Case Western ED 37.06% vs overall 37.78% (ratio 0.98). CWR runs ED1 + ED2 with consistently strong applicant pools; the published ED rate is the binding-pool rate, which is normally below the overall rate that mixes RD volume. Real.
Clarkson ED 75.74% vs overall 82.5% (ratio 0.92). Niche STEM school where overall AR is buoyed by self-selecting STEM applicants in RD; ED pool is small and similar in quality. Real.
Fordham ED 51.6% vs overall 59% (ratio 0.87). Fordham's ED has historically been more selective than RD because the ED pool is dominated by FCRH applicants with stricter academic bars. Real.

NCSU EA 40.21% vs overall 41.33% (ratio 0.97). Public flagship EA pool is roughly the same quality bar as RD; EA serves mainly as deadline preference, not boost. Same pattern as Auburn / Ohio State EA.
Northeastern EA 4.7% vs overall 5.22% (ratio 0.90). Highly selective school where EA pool is at or above RD's bar because EA applicants are mostly the strongest candidates self-selecting. Real.
Ohio State EA 60.43% vs overall 60.57% (ratio 1.00). Public flagship — EA is essentially the same admit bar as RD. Real.
Princeton SCEA 15.82% vs overall 4.42% (ratio 3.58). Real and expected — SCEA pool at T5 is significantly self-selected with stronger profiles. Same pattern as Yale / Harvard SCEA.
Denver ED 76.77% vs overall 77.29% (ratio 0.99). Essentially the same — Denver's overall AR is high and ED pool quality matches. Real.
USF ED 49.41% vs overall 61.71% (ratio 0.80). Niche Jesuit private — overall AR includes broad RD pool; ED pool is more rigorous (similar to Fordham pattern).

RPI ED 58% vs overall 67.25% (ratio 0.86). Real per RPI Class of 2028 (139/240 = 57.9%, corrected in seed-audit-corrections-2026-05-31). RPI's overall AR is already high (~67%), so binding ED is not a competitive lever and admits slightly below the overall rate (same near-AR pattern as Denver / USF). Surfaced once seed-fidelity wiring made the audit ED value win over the stale overlay value (69.09%).
